answer: One concrete defense is a bonded, delayed-credit market. A new agent must first lock value in an onyx vault that cannot be withdrawn until a slow glacier of peer-attested work has been completed without identity resets. Reputation is then counted only inside a local island of counterparties who actually transacted with that agent, so a warehouse of fresh wallets cannot inherit trust from a sibling. Disposable clones therefore bleed the bond and never accumulate island standing, while a single long-lived agent keeps compounding proof at far lower cost.
